title: scania-aps-cost: Cost-Sensitive Machine Learning on Scania APS Failure Data
description:
A reproducible machine-learning study of air pressure system (APS) failure detection in Scania trucks, built on the UCI APS Failure at Scania Trucks dataset (dataset 421).

The project is not organized around maximizing accuracy. It optimizes an explicit industrial objective, the maintenance cost J = 10 × FP + 500 × FN, in which a missed failure is fifty times more expensive than an unnecessary inspection.

The software implements and compares:

  • Model families: regularized logistic regression, linear SVM, random forest, extra trees, XGBoost, LightGBM, a PyTorch MLP, and an autoencoder-plus-classifier.
  • Regularization: L1, L2 and elastic net for linear models; weight decay, dropout, architecture size and early stopping for neural networks; leaf penalties, structural constraints, shrinkage and stochastic subsampling for boosted trees.
  • Optimization: SGD, Adam and AdamW with learning-rate schedules, batch size, gradient clipping and early stopping, retaining epoch-level loss histories.
  • Imbalance handling: class weighting, random undersampling, SMOTE, positive-class weighting and focal loss, with resampling confined to fit-only pipelines.
  • Probability calibration: uncalibrated scores, Platt/sigmoid scaling and isotonic regression, evaluated with Brier score and log loss on a dedicated calibration subset.
  • Threshold optimization: cost-optimal operating points learned on a dedicated threshold subset, including exact optimization over SVM margins rather than treating margins as probabilities.
  • Feature selection and interpretation: L1 embedded sparsity, mutual information, recursive feature elimination, tree-based selection, permutation importance and optional SHAP values.
  • Ablation: component-wise removal of regularization, subsampling, class weighting and cost-optimal thresholding, separating gains in representation from gains in the deployment decision rule.

The experimental protocol splits the official training set into four stratified roles — fit, tune, calibration and threshold — and keeps the official UCI test set outside all of them, so reported costs are not contaminated by model selection, calibration fitting or threshold choice.

The source data is downloaded at runtime and is not redistributed here. It remains subject to its original UCI/Scania terms, which are separate from the MIT license covering this software.
